newsitem.title: INDIA: Bodies of six timber smugglers found in India.
newsitem.headline: Bodies of six timber smugglers found in India.

text.p: Indian police said on Sunday that they had recovered the decomposed remains of six suspected timber smugglers killed by separatist guerrillas in the northeastern state of Assam.
Authorities were searching for the bodies of six other smugglers they believe were shot dead in the same encounter on December 25, they said.
"We suspect the guerrillas fired upon a group of 16 timber smugglers who were ferrying illegal logs in four boats," a senior police official told Reuters in Assam's biggest city, Guwahati.
Twelve of the smugglers were believed to have died while four managed to escape and reported the incident to a nearby military camp. Six of the bodies were discovered on Saturday, police said.
The incident took place at Arunachal Khuti town near Assam's eastern border with Arunachal Pradesh, about 300 km (185 miles) from Guwahati.
Police have identified the victims as Sahami boat people from the eastern state of Bihar.
Assamese guerrillas have been fighting for a separate state since 1079. They accuse the Indian government of exploiting Assam's rich mineral and forest resources.
In November, guerrillas in the tea- and oil-rich state bombed three oil pipelines, forcing two refineries to shut down for a week.
Last week, Bodo tribal militants also seeking a separate state exploded two bombs under a train in Assam, killing at least 33 people.
